data.one_liner: Dart FFI bindings for Linux peripheral I/O (GPIO, I2C, SPI, etc.).
data.what_it_does: Provides Dart wrappers around the c‑periphery library to control hardware peripherals on Linux platforms. It exposes classes for GPIO, LED, PWM, SPI, I2C, MMIO, ADC and serial communication via FFI.
use_when: You need direct access to Linux GPIO, I2C, SPI, PWM, or serial ports from Dart code
Running on a Raspberry Pi or similar SBC and want a Dart‑native API instead of shell commands
avoid_when: Your app must run on non‑Linux platforms (Windows, macOS, web)
You prefer a pure‑Dart implementation without native dependencies
strengths: Thin, close mapping to the well‑tested c‑periphery library
Supports a wide range of peripheral interfaces
Works on popular SBCs like Raspberry Pi, NanoPi, Banana Pi
weaknesses: Linux‑only; cannot be used on other OSes
Requires native library and proper permissions to access /dev devices
Setup can be tricky for beginners unfamiliar with FFI
data.setup_notes: Add the package, ensure the c‑periphery shared library is available on the target device, and grant appropriate permissions to access /dev/* devices (e.g., run as root or adjust udev rules).

alternatives.name: posix
alternatives.why_pick_it: Provides low‑level POSIX system calls for Linux but lacks the high‑level peripheral abstractions of dart_periphery
